We also continue to organise activities to raise staff awareness of environmental protection, explain waste management policies, and encourage staff to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office. Food waste collected daily is transported to an organic resources recovery centre Recycling plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres (one for operations and one for backup). As they account for a major portion of the institution's total energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green design and various energy-saving measures, including in-row cooling systems, LED lighting, and 24-hour monitoring of power usage effectiveness. Following the completion of a consultancy study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations have also begun to obtain green data centre certification. The HKMA recognises the importance of building a culture of sustainability and regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage staff to develop sustainable habits and adopt green and digital working methods. The HKMA shares green living tips and annual office-wide energy and paper consumption statistics with staff, reminding them to help address environmental issues at an individual level; staff are also encouraged to make suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by the Senior Manager of the Administration Division, a task force brings together staff from different departments to brainstorm ideas and propose concrete measures to promote a green working environment. Task force members also act as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages the wider community to adopt more environmentally friendly practices and has launched various initiatives to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry, and the overall economy, minimising resource consumption. The HKMA's "STET" (Secure Transmission of Electronic Returns) system is a one-stop platform for banks to submit documents to the HKMA electronically, covering various periodic returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another system, "e-Delivery", is a secure electronic communication channel for the HKMA to issue information such as circulars and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save a significant amount of paper each year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new generation of management information systems to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) 9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including the issuance of circulars, account opening and closure letters, and responses to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green initiatives, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Faster Payment System (FPS) and stored value facilities, the HKMA encourages the public to adopt electronic payment methods more widely, replacing cash and paper cheques. More information on the FPS and stored value facilities can be found in the chapter "Hong Kong's Role as an International Financial Centre" in the HKMA Annual Report 2022. Sending e-Lai See is simple and convenient, and reduces the use of physical lai see envelopes and banknotes, contributing to Hong Kong's sustainable development. To this end, the HKMA continues to actively promote the use of e-Lai See through various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging the public to send e-Lai See via online or mobile banking services using the FPS or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year period. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organise various activities to attract users to e-Lai See, such as providing festive user interfaces, enhancing features for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cash rebates. The HKMA promotes e-Lai See on social media For members of the public who choose to distribute physical lai see during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "good-as-new" banknotes, i.e. notes that are old but still crisp, for lai see packets. Using good-as-new notes reduces the need to print new banknotes, thereby lessening the environmental impact. Feedback from the note-issuing banks indicates that the public has become increasingly receptive to good-as-new notes in recent years. The Coin Collection Programme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through the programme are recirculated to meet public demand, improving the efficiency of coin circulation and reducing the need for minting. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles, which have served over 1 million people to date, collecting over 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HK$1.3 billion. In 2022, about 78% of users chose to top up their stored value facility accounts with some or all of the value of the coins they exchanged. The HKMA has been collaborating with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying coin collection vehicles on flag-selling days of non-governmental organisations to support social services. Coin counting machine on a coin collection vehicle Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Programme was the world's first systematic coin collection programme using a mobile vehicle concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards, recognising its innovative and environmentally friendly approach to coin handling. The programme operates two coin collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines, to collect coins exchanged by the public. Members of the public can choose to exchange their coins for banknotes, top up their stored value facility accounts (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to the Community Chest for charitable purposes. In addition to collecting coins, the coin collection vehicles are also occasionally deployed for various educational activities (e.g., student visits).

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the climate targets (the “Climate Targets”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The Climate Targets are set with reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual (the “SBTi Corporate Manual”). The purpose of this verification is to confirm whether the Climate Targets are set with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for the purpose of forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Manual. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. Based on the verification results, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets are set with reference to the SBTi Corporate Manual. Shum Siu Yan Audit Supervisor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023 Verification Statement Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the 2022 environmental data (the “2022 Data”) of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the “HKMA”). The 2022 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, and non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate for 2022, as well as the changes in these data compared with the 2015 levels. The HKMA’s GHG emission data are compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the “GHG Protocol”) jointly published by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The scope of verification covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022, and also covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for comparison of annual performance. The scope of verification covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, including 4 offices at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 2 warehouses at 5) Luxson Industrial Centre and 6) Sung Lee Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan respectively. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA’s data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, HKQAA examined representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 6 assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) “Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information” issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for the purpose of forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and checking representative data and information. Relevant original data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of data. Our verification work was conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The HKQAA verification team was not involved in the preparation of the 2022 Data. Based on the verification results, HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are materially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA’s overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu Yan Audit Supervisor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2023

Scaling up and accelerating climate action has become the most pressing issue of our time. We are now almost halfway through the critical decade for climate action. To have a chance of limiting global warming to 1.5°C, we need to cut global carbon emissions by more than 40% this decade. Yet greenhouse gas emissions have hit record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window to keep global temperature rise to 1.5°C is closing fast. We are already feeling the effects of a 1.1°C rise in global temperatures – record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe floods and storms are becoming more frequent and intense around the world. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, we experienced a violent super typhoon, followed immediately by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our good infrastructure and rapid disaster response, the impact was still severe – widespread flooding, transport disruptions and damage to many roads. All this serves as a stark reminder that decisive and ambitious climate action is urgently needed. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We need credible transition strategies that can properly balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is no easy task. The region accounts for more than half of global carbon emissions, driven by rapid economic development and population growth. At the same time, the Asia-Pacific region is densely populated and geographically vulnerable to sea-level rise and extreme weather. Given the different stages of development among economies in the region, the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities for some, but for others, mobilising the necessary transition finance is a huge challenge. The market estimates that the Asia-Pacific region requires over US$3 trillion in low-carbon transition investment annually for the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong has both the capability and the responsibility to leverage the power of finance to support the low-carbon transition across Asia. As a banking regulator, market facilitator and responsible investor, the HKMA has been making significant efforts on the sustainability agenda. You will learn about the specific measures and work the HKMA has undertaken over the past year in the various chapters of this report. In addition, to strengthen the HKMA’s internal governance structure and better coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established a Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For more details on the Steering Committee, please refer to the new chapter on "Governance for Sustainability". Hong Kong banks play a crucial role in supporting Asia’s transition to net zero. In addition to our traditional role as a banking regulator, ensuring that banks properly manage climate risks in our day-to-day supervisory work, we also act as a facilitator, supporting the banking industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green classification framework for consultation in May and are now refining the framework based on feedback received during the consultation. Furthermore, as the demand for higher quality and more globally comparable sustainability disclosures grows, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards launched by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which provide a comprehensive global baseline for sustainability reporting. The HKMA’s role as a facilitator extends beyond developing frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing pain points faced by the industry. Many banks are currently constrained by data limitations in conducting physical risk assessments. To address this, the HKMA will soon launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. Banks will simply need to input a property address to assess the impact of physical hazards on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby helping them manage related climate risks. As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has been playing a bridging role, channelling international investment into sustainable development projects in Asia to support the region’s low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total value of international green and sustainable bonds arranged and issued in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asian market, significantly ahead of other regions. Notably, the Shenzhen Municipal Government and the Hainan Provincial Government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years respectively in 2023, reaffirming Hong Kong’s important role as a green gateway connecting the Mainland with the rest of the world. The vibrant sustainable bond activities in Hong Kong are partly attributable to the demonstration effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$25 billion to institutional and retail investors. We have seized each issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currency, tenor and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world’s largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world’s first tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second issuance of tokenised green bonds; these bonds were denominated in four major currencies and issued in digital native form, making them the world’s first multi-currency digital green bonds. At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong’s sustainable finance ecosystem. These cover a wide range of areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech and transition finance. Particularly in talent development, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Industry in 2023, providing a systematic curriculum for banking practitioners to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of focus for us. It provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors, preventing these sectors from failing to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand the local green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the coverage of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme", which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, thereby encouraging corporates in the region to raise transition funds in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, leveraging public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private sector investment in sustainable development projects that have traditionally been difficult to finance. Some of the above work requires cross-sectoral collaboration and is primarily coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the "Green Banking Alliance", the HKMA’s Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" as a founding member in 2023. Furthermore, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero has announced plans to establish a presence in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channelling of funds to sustainable development projects in the region and globally. To foster new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped organise the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top global decision-makers in business and finance, to discuss ways to scale up climate finance in the region and forge new partnerships. Mr Eddie Yue, Chief Executive of the HKMA, delivering a speech at the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum", a flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week" As the manager of Hong Kong’s official reserves and a significant global asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, gradually expanding the Exchange Fund’s ESG and green asset portfolios in both public and private markets. In line with the target for the Exchange Fund’s "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added a new active global equity portfolio with a sustainability and climate transition theme last year, while also expanding the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public market portfolio. In addition, the HKMA’s priority investments in green, social and sustainability bonds have outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating that it is possible to "do good and do well". In private markets, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund’s equity portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared to 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently been lower than the overall market level. As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement, setting our sustainability goals and plans based on the three pillars of environment, employees and social responsibility. Specifically, on our low-carbon transition journey, we are continuously strengthening our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency improvement and waste management, with the ultimate goal of achieving our commitment to net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the near term and are making good progress towards our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain top talent to fulfil the HKMA’s various important functions, in addition to green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our employees. Furthermore, through collaboration with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing the public’s financial literacy, and raising public awareness of financial fraud. The climate challenge is immense and urgent. Economies around the world are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring about significant changes in financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable risks, but also presents unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to seize the opportunities. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition; continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and sustainable organisation; and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Eddie Yue, Chief Executive

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The HKMA aims to play a leading role in its sustainability efforts through its policies and operations, ensuring that Hong Kong’s financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate change risks and support the transition to a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also contribute to shaping regional and global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As a banking supervisor, the HKMA will further strengthen the climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities of the banking sector. Specifically, key priorities include: conducting a new round of thematic reviews on banks’ climate risk management practices and holding a new round of consultation meetings as part of reviewing banks’ progress in implementing climate risk management regulatory requirements; continuing the work on integrating climate factors into the HKMA’s supervisory review process; completing the second industry-wide climate risk stress test, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including collaborating with local authorities to align relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, which serve as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision’s Pillar 3 framework for climate-related financial vulnerabilities; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the sound development of banks in offering green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to stay abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments and maintain engagement with the industry to ensure banks adopt appropriate sales procedures. In addition, the HKMA will act as a facilitator, driving the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon release a local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities, such as transition activities. At the same time, we will continue to explore the use of technology solutions to help banks identify, measure, and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming cloud-based platform to facilitate banks’ physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional capabilities of practitioners, we will also develop the “Green and Sustainable Finance” module at the professional level under the “Banking Professional Qualifications Framework” in 2024. Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the recommendations of the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme to cover sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable debt market; and attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance, to Hong Kong through the “Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme”. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and corporations to raise green funds through Hong Kong and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in implementing the government-funded “Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme” to expand Hong Kong’s green finance talent pool. As co-chair of the “Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group” (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and efforts to promote the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus on three key areas: sustainable disclosures, technology application, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the “Green Commercial Banking Alliance”, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help financial institutions establish their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen cooperation with the “Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero”, the “Capacity Building Coalition for Sustainable Investment”, and the “Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership”. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the “Investment Portfolio” of the Exchange Fund by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund’s investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio in the journey towards net zero. Recognising that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a whole-economy transition, we are refining our net-zero strategy to focus on assets that deliver positive climate benefits for the real economy, while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally supportive institution, the HKMA’s decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve to reflect the latest developments in markets, regulations, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA’s climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our office premises. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage our staff to participate in our sustainability efforts, including launching campaigns to cultivate sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers’ ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the specified certification standards. For the periodic renewal of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and consolidation, and actively modernise internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimise potential risks. Finally, in terms of social focus areas, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable development organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the broader Asian region. The HKMA has a robust sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures the integration of sustainability factors into the HKMA's own operations and practices. Committed to good institutional governance, the HKMA has established a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This governance framework ensures the effective integration of sustainability factors into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and includes effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainable development efforts. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialist committees, which oversee and advise on the HKMA's work, including its sustainable development efforts; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, which leads the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and for other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups plan and implement sustainability measures related to banking, market development, and the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-founded by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's various sustainable development efforts in recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development work across the HKMA's different functional areas¹. It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters in four functional areas: banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA's Chief Executive, with three Deputy Chief Executives as standing members. We also invite relevant Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key achievements and future plans for their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Department, and Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-founded the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020². The Steering Group serves as a cross-institutional platform, providing strategic direction and coordinating cross-sectoral work on climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Steering Group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their daily business operations. To continue playing their important role in the financial system and channel more funds into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the banking regulator, the HKMA is particularly focused on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risk, and accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking system's resilience to climate risk. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the economy's transition to net-zero emissions. Following this circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey on selected banks in Q4 to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate experience sharing among the industry. On disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) consultation in November on a Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is stepping up its efforts to refine the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided advice to banks to help them further enhance their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing a two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process. Climate risk management is now a standing agenda item in prudential supervisory meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors have also adopted an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing the two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking supervisory process, the HKMA revised the "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risk. Key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023 Following the end of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with the Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA launched a thematic review on climate-related risk governance in Q2. This thematic review covered four major areas: climate-related risk governance structure, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made several enhancements to the climate risk stress testing framework, including introducing a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of simultaneous economic and climate change shocks. Following these enhancements and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisory-led stress testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress tests commenced in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance banks' capacity to manage climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, an increase of over 60% compared to the first pilot exercise in 2021. The HKMA also held a climate risk stress testing forum in November, which was attended by up to 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating experience sharing among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other public information to assess their progress. The HKMA provided targeted advice to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As global attention on climate change and efforts to address it increase, the HKMA has noted a growing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering such products to meet customer needs. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sales of green and sustainable investment products and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to meet and sharing observed good practices. This circular covers areas such as product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and book-building, aiming to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, enhancing banks' ability to manage climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot cloud platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulatory authorities to explore how technology solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby strengthening banks' sustainable processes for submitting AML-related data. In September, the HKMA organised a "Green Fintech Competition" to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 entries from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held a "Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar", providing a platform for the banking industry and the technology sector to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green fintech in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and the Mainland, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition". The event attracted around 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory authorities and academia. To enhance transparency among financial markets and align green and sustainable finance decisions, the HKMA, with the assistance of a consultancy firm, developed a local green classification framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Hong Kong Green Classification Framework Prototype", seeking stakeholder views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which has recognised environmental crime as a predicate offence for money laundering, and this area is receiving increasing attention from regulators due to the linkage between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors. Recognising that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial vulnerability analysis and research to enhance its ongoing surveillance work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interaction between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, allowing policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. On the research front, the HKMA has conducted several applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial industry and the economy. Research topics include climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains5. The findings of these studies have enhanced the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, aiding in policy formulation. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA shares research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international activities on climate-related matters and the HKMA Research Memoranda. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a secured standby liquidity arrangement providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework, as recommended by the NGFS. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and promoting sustainable finance as a mainstream issue. Through this engagement, the HKMA helps facilitate policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerates the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supports the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with major work areas including sustainable disclosure, ecosystem enhancement, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Working Group has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group has also been set up to explore ways to support financial institutions and corporates in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group is also strengthening the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. Particularly in data, we continue to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies, launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's status as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key workstreams to capture the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To facilitate skills training in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance, under the Steering Group, implemented the Government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme", providing subsidies for practitioners, students, and graduates who undergo green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched the basic level of a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the industry. To help financial institutions and corporates, especially small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, the HKMA, during the year, collaborated with relevant government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. For students, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen the understanding of sustainable finance among interns and university bachelor's degree graduates. Recognising the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and improving its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancements to provide a one-stop shop for green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, corporates, and the public. Key enhancements include a sustainable disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralised, easy-to-navigate, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group, together with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong, co-organised the "Leveraging Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporates, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The highlight of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top global decision-makers in business and finance, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, heavy industry decarbonisation, circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets in the Asia-Pacific region. The forum received responses from public and private institutions, co-organising over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other networking events. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition finance, green finance taxonomy, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024, discussing key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These activities are part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as useful platforms to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting green and sustainable finance development in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance", a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second cutting-edge research report titled "Developing Ambitious Climate Strategies in Green Banking: Case Studies". During the year, the HKMA Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Coalition for Capacity Building on Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the Green Development International Alliance under the Belt and Road Initiative. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will help build capacity and share knowledge, and channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter, which will help support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA assists GFANZ's work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's commitment to combating climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in issuing green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately US$25 billion equivalent in green institutional and retail bonds, with the proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the programme's transparency and accountability, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report", detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bond issuances and the expected environmental benefits. The Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance in the 2023-24 financial year, issuing approximately US$6 billion equivalent in green bonds in June. This triple-currency offering covered bonds of different tenors in US dollars, euros, and renminbi, attracting a diverse range of investors, with subscription demand being strong, recording nearly US$30 billion equivalent in subscriptions. The issuance amount of renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was issued for the first time, helping to extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore renminbi (CNH) product choices. The enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued a second batch of green retail bonds totalling HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and fostering inclusive finance. This issuance provided the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a key role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to proactively exercise asset ownership and integrate environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preservation of capital first, long-term growth thereafter"1, believing that adequate attention to ESG factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "Net Zero 2050" target2 for its "Investment Portfolio", the HKMA is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment in the financial industry and central banking community. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is dedicated to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Chart 1 The Exchange Fund's responsible investment journey Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero goals. To fulfil its commitments to the Glasgow Declaration3 of the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) and the strategic plan of the Cross-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, the HKMA has prepared this chapter on the Exchange Fund's responsible investment in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principles set the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, oversees ESG and climate-related risks in Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and monitors ESG efforts across the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets semi-annually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. Chart 2 Responsible investment governance structure of the Exchange Fund Investment Office As shown in Chart 1, the Exchange Fund Investment Office began its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability rapidly evolved and became a strategic priority for major institutions globally beyond risk considerations, the Exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the Exchange Fund Investment Office establishing a new Business Strategy Division led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the dedicated responsible investment team formerly under the Risk Management and Monitoring Division – now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic move reflects the HKMA's shift in the focus of responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investments. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams in the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different investment types: Public Market Investments – The Credit, Regulation and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Division. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (see "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private Market Investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers ESG-related assessments for each investment proposal made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams. The HKMA recognises that physical and transition risks4 from climate change, as well as related opportunities, affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2023"5 projects that unless global greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological developments or behavioural changes to control temperature rise may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in ESG integration. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2050, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. The following sections will elaborate on this approach. Chart 3 The HKMA's three-pronged approach to responsible investment In progressing towards the net-zero target, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial for achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential impacts on investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition, including those in high-emission industries, that possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to navigate changing global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding such investments or divesting does not help solve the carbon emission problem. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, the HKMA supports these industries, driving them to implement transitions to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about positive change for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net-zero investment strategy, adopting a comprehensive approach to achieve transition outcomes aligned with the Exchange Fund's and global net-zero goals, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to promote climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Chart 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new active global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another portfolio managed by an external investment manager. Additionally, the HKMA prioritised investments in green, social and sustainability bonds, which outperformed their investment benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing good while doing well". In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Chart 4 Ongoing measures to promote ESG investments The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing environmentally friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature processes to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material serves as a sustainable and versatile alternative to oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and consumer durables. Additionally, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies like 3D printing. The company is a strong advocate of the circular economy. The chart below illustrates the positive environmental outcomes of its advanced plastic production process: The MCPP, managed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), is an innovative initiative that combines institutional investor capital with the IFC's own funds to scale up sustainable financing for private companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed US$1 billion each to two tranches of the MCPP in 2017 and 2019, and further collaborated with the IFC in 2021 to create a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet", which is also the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to the IFC's report, the HKMA's loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in various areas, including economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, projects financed by the HKMA's loans are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gases emitted by an average petrol car travelling 14 billion miles. Chart 5 Projected average annual benefits of the HKMA's loan commitments to the MCPP since 2020 The green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capacity.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, taking a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also focuses on employee well-being and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial knowledge. As a responsible institution, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee)¹, established in October and chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is the primary decision-making body for various institutional sustainability initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies for institutional sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Deputy Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and reports progress to the Steering Committee regularly. The Green Office Box and the Volunteer Service Team provide support for coordinating institutional sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming ideas on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of volunteer participation. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation journey. The focus is on implementing carbon reduction strategies in its daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly working modes, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to use carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and employ carbon offsetting measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to its daily operations, the HKMA continues to roll out more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, the HKMA hires a professional team, builds a talent pool, and focuses on employee well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers the selection of social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes financial consumer education; and collaborates with the banking industry to ensure fair access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter sets out the details of each of the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee², chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, may affect the HKMA's offices and impede staff travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The office designs also incorporate various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel, and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring its exposure to transition risks by tracking its greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) across all categories of its institutional operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the base year, reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach within practical limits to minimise greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 3 (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets are formulated with reference to the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify its emission, energy consumption, paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report⁶. The scope and basis of verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the *2022 Annual Report*, the HKMA also published its first standalone *2022 Sustainability Report*. The HKMA's efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognised with an ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulatory institution to receive an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for achieving good ESG standards, finding the *Sustainability Report* clear and easy to read, and noting that appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high transparency and accountability in reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA also received the highest rating of Gold Award in the "Non-Profit and Charitable Organisations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Report Awards 2023". The judging panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, employees, and the community at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Company" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations, and its internal *Green Office Guidelines* provide guidance to staff on resource use and office waste generation. The HKMA has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating offices, existing furniture and finishing materials are reused as much as possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly building and decorative materials are given priority. The HKMA has consistently followed this practice, resulting in Gold certification under LEED⁷ and "BEAM Plus Interior"⁸ for parts of its renovated offices in Two International Finance Centre in 2021 and 2022, respectively. Adopting new technologies and making good use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains a key focus for the HKMA. In addition to promoting good habits, such as turning off unnecessary lighting in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using LED lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning room temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimising energy use in the IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has been continuously decreasing, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours per person⁹ in 2023, a decrease of 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions primarily come from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined density of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per person¹⁰, a decrease of 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardised equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the HKMA also adopts digital tools and technologies, and automates and streamlines workflows to build a digital working environment and enhance online collaboration within the institution.¹¹ Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meeting for the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative matters are primarily handled through electronic processes. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working modes, replacing paper documents and communications with digital methods. At the same time, work is underway to implement an electronic records management system. The above green and digital initiatives have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption density in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international activities have resumed in physical format following the COVID-19 pandemic, and to promote Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is unavoidable that relevant HKMA staff need to travel overseas for business. To reduce the carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to take direct flights or combine different business trips where feasible when participating in overseas activities. At the institutional level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO₂e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel.
