In addition, the HKMA participates in a carbon offset programme certified under the "Gold Standard"¹² to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this programme involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and providing efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process considers sustainability and environmental factors. As part of a comprehensive review of the institution's procurement policies and procedures, the existing practice of procuring green products has been formalised, following the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", especially in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that enhance productivity and efficiency have been added to the bid evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. Following the "4R" principle, i.e., Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated for the first time directly in the red packet recycling programme of the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Staff collectively contributed approximately 3,000 used but still intact red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operations and backup data centres are a major part of the institution's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)¹³. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment guide issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has been a key focus of the technical team. To this end, the team has adopted green designs in renovation works and implemented energy-efficient good practices to lower PUE and achieve related targets, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centre's environmental facilities and continuously improving environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continuously improves the energy use of the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in all aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. The HKMA also began preparations shortly after the study's completion to obtain "Green Data Centre" certification under the "BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process was very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team implemented optimisation measures based on the recommendations of the consultant's report to enhance energy performance and even the health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data"). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, business air travel greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), their respective intensities, and the changes in these data compared to 2015 levels. In addition, the 2023 Data also includes the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when the HKMA began its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste). The verification scope covers a total of five office and warehouse assets, of which four offices are located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located at 5) Luxor Industrial Centre, Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the five assets. This verification was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information", issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanism, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and checking selected representative data and information. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work was absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team did not participate in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data is substantially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin Head of Assurance Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat of climate change is imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed 2024 as the hottest year on record, and the first year in which global temperatures exceeded the critical 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, global greenhouse gas emissions, which had moderated slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, have recently hit new highs, highlighting the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. In the process of addressing global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Moreover, the current tense geopolitical landscape, the increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, the heightened concerns over energy security, and the uncertain economic outlook all pose greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, the transition challenge is most acute in Asia. As the World Economic Forum points out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a crucial role in the global success of achieving net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centre in Asia, Hong Kong must strengthen its leading role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive the regional transition. To this end, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating sustainable development principles into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on enhancing the financial industry's ability to manage climate change-related risks on the one hand, and on assisting the industry in seizing related new opportunities on the other. At the same time, we lead by example. The HKMA's sustainable development work covers four major areas: supporting the banking system in moving towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a key role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Asia, but it also faces numerous risks during the transition process. In the "Action Plan", we set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and to achieve net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. At the same time, we require all banks to enhance their disclosure of climate change-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance on banks' transition planning to help them enhance their capacity to cope with the transition and better manage related risks. We are also working with relevant stakeholders on preparatory work to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further enhance the industry's transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are refining the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification Taxonomy, launched in May last year, to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investments. However, it also presents opportunities for the Exchange Fund to grow and generate positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainable impact can be mutually reinforcing, with no inherent conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and pledged in the "Action Plan" to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for over 10% of the "Investment Portfolio". To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year, aiming to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in Asia through co-investment. Furthermore, we published the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document in September last year to further promote active stewardship and good sustainable investment practices among fund managers. Capital mobilisation is particularly important for accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including Mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays a vital role in channelling capital to accelerate the regional transition. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable development financing platform and the goal of promoting sustainable financial innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to promote green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to cover transition financing instruments in May last year, and launching the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November last year, we have been consistently encouraging regional issuers to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise funds needed for decarbonisation and transition. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem for support. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry talent with relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, we pledged in the "Action Plan" to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures and to work towards filling the gap in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosures, particularly by providing easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosures among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). We also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework in November last year to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Additionally, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we engaged various stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Internally at the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring our operations align with the vision of sustainable development. We pledged in the "Action Plan" to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or earlier, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the government. We began using electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement processes. At the same time, we continue to enhance work efficiency through digitalisation, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organisation, and motivate employees to actively participate in sustainable development efforts. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic geopolitical changes have added variables to global climate action. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is gradually intensifying. In the work to address climate change, the current situation does not allow for any slackening. We firmly believe that promoting an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system and bring us opportunities in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, diligently advancing our sustainable development work and deepening our relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges, we remain committed, as always, to supporting the building of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge of our time. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development in Asia and globally. In October 2024, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving our targets, and how we expect the industry to work together to drive related efforts. Through formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory engagement, and enhancing internal operations, the HKMA plans to bolster the resilience of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself against climate change risks, and to promote the transition to a more sustainable economy in Asia. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA also aims to exert influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the transition to net zero. Our priorities for 2025 include: - launching a new round of thematic review on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation meetings to review banks' implementation of the HKMA's relevant regulatory requirements and further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - refining the work to incorporate climate risk stress tests into the HKMA's supervisory-led stress testing framework; - continuing to advance the work of integrating climate factors into the HKMA's Supervisory Review Process; - commencing preparatory work for formulating regulatory requirements on the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) for the local banking sector; - completing the drafting of new module GS-2 of the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - sharing good practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to its role as a banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, committed to driving the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing transition finance. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification Taxonomy", providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitate related capital flows. The HKMA has commenced the second phase of the taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will organise another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support the region's sustainable financing needs. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme", the expanded scope of which will include sustainable projects, such as social projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration effect for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies under the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies for prospective issuers of digital green bonds under the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme". Although there is a growing market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and corporates, the capabilities and readiness of different entities to make sustainable disclosures vary, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with more climate disclosure-related tools, including easy-to-use sustainable disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how technology can be used to make existing resources more user-friendly; and collaborate with key local industry organisations to provide the training needed by the industry. The sustainable finance market is evolving rapidly, requiring the expansion of the local talent pool and addressing knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key work in 2025 includes collaborating with the banking industry to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework", and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the forthcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its scope of application. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance" to launch special initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted upskilling and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, to support the overall economic transition. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability. In response to the accelerated timeline for achieving net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan", the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting at a pragmatic pace, continuing to drive the institution's sustainable development. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on material topics. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the significant impact of climate risk on our offices and operations, to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government's published "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrades based on energy efficiency and conservation principles. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainable development organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the broader Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of measures, and ensure that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working methods. Committed to good institutional governance, the HKMA has built a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, with effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainable development efforts. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework includes: - The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialist committees, which oversee and advise on the HKMA's work, including its sustainable development efforts; - The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; - In the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - For other functional areas, relevant groups and working groups plan and implement sustainability measures related to banking, market development, and the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-founded by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the work of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the HKMA's various sustainable development efforts over the past years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters across four functional areas: banking, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's functional departments; - Assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG targets; and - Overseeing external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, with three Deputy Chief Executives as standing members. We also invite dedicated Executive Directors from key functions related to green and sustainable development matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on key achievements and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA co-founded the Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-institutional platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral work on climate and environmental risks in the financial industry, to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system against climate risk, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their daily business operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risk. At the same time, banks play a crucial role in the financial system by channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risk, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Plan" comprises eight targets across four areas. To help the industry achieve the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. All banks are to increase transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft of Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-2 "Transition Planning". The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to address net-zero transition and related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the Supervisory Review Process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) for effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risk. The HKMA has been working to align local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the BCBS's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Plan". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification (Taxonomy) to address industry concerns about greenwashing and help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, aiming to align with common green taxonomies and those of Mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating local elements. We have commenced the second phase to expand the Taxonomy's coverage and are consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and supported banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risk into the banking supervisory process. To promote banks' capacity to enhance climate risk management, the HKMA shared with the banking industry good practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings, including: - Establishing a robust governance structure with clearly defined responsibilities for the board and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA held a balanced regulatory roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and supported the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA conducted a round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" and understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided bank-specific feedback and guidance to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, involving 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. The results showed that under various scenarios (including those assuming simultaneous climate risk and macroeconomic downside), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot, participating banks significantly improved their capacity to measure and assess climate risk. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA recognises the numerous challenges banks face in climate risk management regarding data and methodologies, and has therefore been undertaking various initiatives to promote the use of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform based on user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborates with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we published a practical application guide and two "Regtech Use Case Briefs" (English versions), describing technology solutions for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessment, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA recognises that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and therefore incorporates a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial vulnerability analysis and research to enhance ongoing surveillance. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps further enrich climate scenarios, aiding central banks and regulators in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. In November, the NGFS released the fifth vintage of long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessments. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interaction between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to take a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. The HKMA published a "Practical Guide on Green Technology Application for Banks" (English version), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. In research, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the broader economy. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in buffering against monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The findings not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding policy formulation. Domestically, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of climate change's impact on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the "HKMA Research Memoranda". The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (HKIMR), the research arm of the Hong Kong Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can benefit significantly from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study is featured in the HKIMR's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a secured backstop liquidity facility providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and promoting sustainable finance as mainstream. Through this engagement, we help facilitate policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability at the international and regional levels, and draw lessons to enhance the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As articulated in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), the HKMA is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial market, enhancing the industry's sustainable disclosures, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalysing sustainable finance innovation Supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures Filling the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing a total of approximately US$28 billion equivalent in green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We seize each issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currency, tenor, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the Programme's scope was expanded to cover sustainable projects and was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes the "Green Bond Report" on a year-on-year basis, detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing approximately US$3 billion equivalent of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This triple-currency offering comprised bonds in renminbi (RMB), US dollars (USD), and euros (EUR) across different tenors. These bonds attracted participation from various types of investors, with strong subscription demand, recording over US$15 billion equivalent in subscription amounts. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds were the Government's first issuance of such tenors, representing the longest-tenor RMB bonds issued by the Government to date, setting a new benchmark for the market and further demonstrating the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the range of offshore renminbi (CNH) investment products in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers in the region to utilise Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable development funds, the HKMA continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in May 2021, providing subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The Scheme has been well received by the industry. As of the end of 2024, the Scheme had approved subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion. The Scheme was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, and its scope was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the Scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilise Hong Kong's transition financing platform to gradually decarbonise. - Approved subsidies for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total value exceeding US$140 billion (as of the end of 2024) - Extended for three years to 2027, with the scope of subsidies expanded to cover transition financing instruments Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promotes Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and these efforts have yielded positive results. Notably, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, with a total value of RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 0.9 billion in social bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable capital between Mainland China and the rest of the world. Leveraging these various measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, in 2024, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with a total volume of such bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region in applying asset digitalisation and innovative technologies in the field of green and sustainable finance. The HKMA also launched the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" in November to promote digital bond issuances in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovative development in Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market. The working group on sustainable disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group) has been making efforts towards Hong Kong's adoption of the "International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards" (ISSB Standards). The Government published the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" in December 2024, providing a clear pathway for large public accountability entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of preparation in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosures, making sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the application of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies" (Questionnaire) launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainable disclosures by enterprises, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024, making it convenient for enterprises to complete online (see QR code below). The HKMA is optimising the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly. Specific measures include selecting core questions from the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios for the Questionnaire. Additionally, we aim to improve the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its "Sustainability Report" in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as its plans and progress towards achieving climate goals. For details on sustainable disclosures related to our own operations, please refer to the "Sustainable HKMA" chapter. Given the rapidly evolving sustainable finance market, to address knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking industry and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulatory bodies and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the basic level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023. This module aims to assist banking professionals in acquiring knowledge and developing professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, covering four main areas of work: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable/climate risk management; (3) sustainable disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance, and governance. Furthermore, the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting mid-to-senior level banking practitioners responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide necessary training to banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the managing body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the basic level training course for the module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop training courses for the professional level. To understand further skills and training needs in the banking industry, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking industry on a study on "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030", with the aim of publishing the results in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent 2021-2025" document published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide important reference for the industry, helping it to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking industry. The HKMA, through its collaboration with the Steering Group, also continues to assist in implementing the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme", which subsidises practitioners, graduates, and students to receive training related to sustainable finance. As of December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses had been registered as eligible training courses under the Scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the "2025-26 Budget" that the Scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions covering global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative instruments. Additionally, the HKMA supported the establishment of a branch office of the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to enhance skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads green and sustainable finance development. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA adheres to responsible investment principles in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. The HKMA invests prudently under the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term growth", believing that adequate attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment efforts. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve better risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Chart 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document publicly available to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly set industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment in the financial industry and among central banks. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainability go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), further consolidating its commitment to investing in a sustainable future by setting a target of achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2050 for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" and mobilising partners to support the low-carbon economic transition. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to balance responsible investment practices with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team under the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Chart 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, coordinates and monitors ESG efforts across the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive and attended by the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office and the Chief Strategy Officer, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams in the Exchange Fund Investment Office on ESG integration and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across investment types: - Public market investments – The Credit, Regulatory and Monitoring Committee, composed of senior management of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with input from the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG profile of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Monitoring Department. Additionally, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers for equity portfolios from an ESG perspective (see "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 39 for details). - Private market investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, considers ESG-related assessments for each investment proposal made by the private market investment and risk management teams. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks and related opportunities arising from climate change can affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investments. The United Nations Environment Programme's "Emissions Gap Report 2024" projects that, unless there is a large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts to address rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries towards sustainable solutions also creates investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure that may offer attractive long-term prospects. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in ESG integration. The HKMA has set a target of achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2050 for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this target (see Chart 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Plan", which consolidates the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Chart 4). To support the low-carbon economic transition, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable projects. Investing in a sustainable future: Net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio" by or before 2050 - Actively expand the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with special attention to climate change and transition prospects - Establish clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply - Aim to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by or before 2030 Supporting regional transition through investment - Continue to engage with external investment managers to optimise transition-enhancing investment opportunities - Continue to identify and prioritise high-quality investment opportunities that promote Asia's transition and generate positive global impact First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the primary investment objective of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, with potential implications for investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition, including those in high-emission industries, that possess excellent technology and good corporate governance to navigate changing global climate trends. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding related investments or divesting does not help solve carbon emission problems. Instead, by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, the HKMA supports these industries in transitioning to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby generating positive changes for themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, driving comprehensive decarbonisation across the economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of a portfolio depends not only on its own adjustments but also on broad economic transition. Although there is no single perfect solution, the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero goals of the Exchange Fund and the world. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including ESG integration and stewardship in fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investments in assets aligned with pathways to net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting portfolios towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, it may focus more on transition-enhancing investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's "Investment Portfolio", with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Chart 5). - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of customised low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the case study in the "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" section). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capturing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and reviews investment opportunities that can accelerate energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (see examples in the "Joining Forces to Address Climate Challenges in Asia and Globally" section). - Passive investment portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios using non-ESG indices as investment benchmarks - Active investment portfolios with a governance theme - Active ESG investment portfolios with sustainability and climate transition themes - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds focused on energy transition and decarbonisation in global, Asian and Global South markets - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The "Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program" (MCPP) managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" project, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement The HKMA invests in green bonds issued by a quasi-government agency. The proceeds from the green bonds are allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading ageing equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrades encompass optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to ongoing wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or repurpose dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also use gas generated from the sludge treatment process to fuel boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invests in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds finance multiple projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water from rivers to arid regions. The main objective of the project is to repair the deteriorating canal lining to prevent leakage, conserve water, improve water efficiency and reclaim waterlogged areas. Additionally, the project conducts skills training for local stakeholders to promote the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable institution. One of its key work priorities in 2024 to fulfil this commitment is to plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than the original target, in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and well-being, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is the main decision-making body for various institutional sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee in October 2024 approved a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions in its own operations by or before 2030, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Executive Director (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to institutional operations, staff well-being, and social connectivity, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on institutional sustainability measures. The Green Office Box and Volunteer Service Team, comprising staff from different operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing ideas on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff, and the wider community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Company" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to adopt a structure based on three pillars: environmental, staff, and social responsibility. - Focus on decarbonising and digitalising the HKMA's daily operations, with a target to achieve net-zero emissions by or before 2030 - Adopt green procurement requirements in line with government guidelines - Promote greener operational solutions to the financial industry and the wider community - Build a positive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Foster a collaborative, caring, and inclusive working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Provide a quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle - Cultivate a culture of caring for the community - Incorporate social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management - Promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy through consumer education activities The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own operations to 2030, 20 years earlier than its original commitment, as part of the "Action Plan". The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for electricity generation by local power companies. Additionally, the HKMA is establishing a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency and simultaneously reduce its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognising the importance of fostering a culture of sustainability, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the primary target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and procuring low-carbon options where possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from its air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programmes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the above environmental commitments related to its physical operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and the return of collected coins to circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, promoting staff well-being, and caring for the community. Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To better assess the potential impact of climate change on its operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the HKMA's office design incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. Additionally, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures covering not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff are always prepared to implement response measures. The HKMA also monitors its exposure to transition risks by tracking its operational greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions related to its own operations across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 by or before 2030. These targets are set with reference to the "Science Based Targets initiative" methodology. The HKMA uses the "Greenhouse Gas Protocol" to measure and report its institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect emissions from electricity generated by fossil fuel consumption. In the absence of individual supplier data, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate its main Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculations for 2023 and 2024 are presented in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of this verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" appended to this report. The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it monitors to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve full green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, during various renovation projects in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and renovation materials or traded them in for new items, reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in its offices and data centres. In 2024, as part of the data centre facility upgrade project, the HKMA adopted a modular design for the uninterruptible power supply system to further optimise the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial loads, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA enhances internal virtual collaboration through its digital workplace, streamlining workflows and effectively reducing paper consumption. Additionally, the HKMA extends the useful life of its mobile and desktop devices in line with manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated in its offices, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles, namely refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has placed recycling bins for different materials in multiple convenient locations in its offices. To improve recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit net bags in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has been sending its collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Pledge", committing to take measures to reduce waste generated from its various activities. The HKMA continues to prioritise the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to carefully plan their itineraries, for example, by combining multiple trips when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, since 2023, the HKMA has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel, reducing approximately 10% of its annual carbon emissions from air travel. Additionally, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard" certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from its air travel; this programme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged various learning activities for staff, such as seminars and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" from Earth Day on 22 April 2024 throughout May, with the theme "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a good opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA's commitment and drive to implement environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to practice green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and a "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan; it also shared waste audit results and introduced best practices for recycling by a community recycling centre operator. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign in October lasting approximately six months, highlighting responsible waste management and reminding staff that the aggregation of small changes in their individual habits can significantly enhance the overall institutional recycling performance. A highlight of the campaign was the launch of a "Green Action" video series, where several senior executives shared recycling tips. The campaign also featured a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to encourage staff to reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their understanding of sustainability and gather their views on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help inform the development of future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA sees itself as a key agent of change and is therefore committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable practices in the financial industry and the wider community. The HKMA has launched several measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded its service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The aim of expanding the platform's service scope is to further streamline the submission process for reporting entities, providing a smoother experience for all users, while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new initiatives launched in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys using a simplified submission process, and a smart information and document management system, providing users with a central platform for advanced search functions related to bank-related documents.

Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has conducted independent verification of the environmental data ("Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel in 2024, together with their respective densities. In addition, the data also includes Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting in 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding densities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data has been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, of which 5 offices are located in 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, 5) The International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located in 6) Luxsonor Industrial Centre, Kwai Chung. The objective of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the verification scope, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has reviewed selected representative data and supporting evidence from the 6 assets. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to obtain a reasonable level of assurance for forming an opinion and conclusion. The verification process was carried out in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to its source, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation and internal checks, and performed reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the data, and checking selected representative data and information. Relevant original data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team has not participated in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance on the Data and concludes that: - The Data is substantively accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Suki Siu Audit Manager Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
